summary: Archived design samples for thoughtful play after Level 60. They remain outside the runtime level sequence and the permanent database.

levels.title: The Long Way Out
levels.difficultyIntent: Teach the player to inspect several exit lanes before touching the first available car.
designRules: The fifth red car stays behind two police blockers and the upper blue limousine.
At least three cars look movable at the start, but only the blue-side route opens the short dependency chain.
No timer or hidden information is used.
intendedStrategy: Trace the blue limousine exit lane before selecting a color.
Remove the two police blockers that release the center route.
Delay committing four red cars until the fifth red route is visible.
successCriteria: The player can explain which blocker releases the fifth red car.
The level remains solvable without using the extra-slot booster.

levels.title: Four Is Not Five
levels.difficultyIntent: Create an attractive near-match that punishes filling the tray without locating the final matching car.
designRules: Four red cars are immediately reachable while the fifth red car is behind the green limousine.
A tempting yellow car can fill the final tray bay before the fifth red becomes available.
The side parking bay provides the recovery route and should be visually emphasized once.
intendedStrategy: Count all five red cars before committing to the near-match.
If the yellow car is selected, park it before releasing the fifth red.
Clear red, then return the parked yellow car.
successCriteria: The intended solution uses parking at least once.
There is no forced heart loss when the player reads the board correctly.

levels.title: Valet Exchange
levels.difficultyIntent: Turn the side bay into a planned temporary storage tool instead of an emergency button.
designRules: The intended solution deliberately chains five side-bay entries.
The parking-use counter displays 5 at the start and decreases only when a car enters the side bay.
The board remains solvable with exactly the five entries used by its validated route.
intendedStrategy: Use the side bay before committing the first full color group.
Swap parked interruptions only when the next five-car route is visible.
Complete the final color with no parking uses remaining.
successCriteria: All five parking uses form part of the validated solution route.
The player cannot bypass the lesson with the extra-slot booster.

levels.title: Key Color
levels.difficultyIntent: Introduce a clearly communicated lock that opens after a visible color goal is completed.

locks.presentation: Red car displays a green padlock badge and the status strip points toward the green goal.

designRules: The locked red car cannot be tapped until the green group clears.
The lock condition is always visible on the car and beside the tracker.
Tapping the locked car gives informational feedback and does not remove a heart.
intendedStrategy: Recognize that green is the key color.
Clear the green group while keeping enough tray space for the unlocked red route.
Use the newly unlocked red car to release the lower-right lane.
successCriteria: The first lock is understandable without written instructions.
A locked-car tap never counts as a mistake.

levels.title: Traffic Schedule
levels.difficultyIntent: Make players plan several matches ahead by displaying a required color-completion order.
designRules: The tracker displays the four goal colors as a left-to-right sequence.
Cars of later colors may enter the tray, but they cannot clear before their turn.
Selecting a later color is a strategic choice and does not directly cost a heart.
intendedStrategy: Complete red before committing the green route.
Preserve adjacent tray positions when blue becomes the third goal.
Finish with yellow after the board has opened.
successCriteria: The displayed order is readable at phone size.
The level remains solvable without hiding or changing any car direction.

levels.title: Rush-Hour Finale
levels.difficultyIntent: Combine familiar systems into a difficult but fully readable planning puzzle.

locks.presentation: Red car uses a green padlock badge.
Yellow car uses a red padlock badge.

designRules: Two limousines form the central dependency chain.
Four parking entries are used at different stages of the ordered goals.
Green unlocks red; red unlocks yellow; all relationships remain visible.
No timer, random blocker, or hidden direction is allowed.
intendedStrategy: Clear the green route around the first limousine and unlock red.
Use parking swaps to preserve the red and yellow sequences.
Finish yellow, then preserve adjacent positions for blue.
successCriteria: Every mechanic was introduced in an earlier sample before this combination.
The intended solution uses exactly four parking entries and no booster.
All locks and goal dependencies are visible before the first move.
